import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 2.40

by A. I. Mal'cev

c) The *$I$-theory* (*$Q$-theory*) of a class $\mathfrak{K}$ of universal algebras is the
totality of all identities (quasi-identities) that are valid on all algebras in $\mathfrak{K}$.
Does there exist a finitely axiomatizable variety (3) of Lie rings (i) whose $I$-theory is
non-decidable?

*Remark* (from the notebook): it is not difficult to find a recursively axiomatizable variety of
semigroups with identity whose $I$-theory is non-recursive (see also A. I. Mal'cev,
*Mat. Sbornik*, **69**, no. 1 (1966), 3–12 (Russian)).

The labels (3) and (i) are the notebook's item numbers. Only this item of Problem 2.40 is still
open; the other parts and items of the problem have been solved and are not stated here.

## Formalisation

* A Lie ring is a `LieRing` in the sense of Mathlib: an additive commutative group with a
  biadditive bracket that vanishes on the diagonal and satisfies the Jacobi (Leibniz) identity,
  i.e. a Lie algebra over $\mathbb{Z}$.
* `LieTerm` is the type of terms in the signature $(0, -, +, [\,\cdot,\cdot\,])$ of Lie rings,
  with variables $x_0, x_1, x_2, \dots$ indexed by `ℕ`. An *identity* is a pair of terms
  $(s, t)$, read as the universally quantified equation $s = t$; it *holds* in a Lie ring $L$
  if $s$ and $t$ take the same value in $L$ under every assignment of the variables.
* The *variety* defined by a set $S$ of identities is the class of Lie rings in which every
  identity of $S$ holds (`variety`); it is *finitely axiomatizable* when $S$ is finite.
* The *$I$-theory* of a class $\mathfrak{K}$ of Lie rings is the set of identities that hold in
  every member of $\mathfrak{K}$ (`iTheory`). The class is quantified over Lie rings in `Type`;
  for identities this loses nothing, since an identity that fails in some Lie ring already
  fails in the countable Lie subring generated by the witnesses.
* Decidability is Mathlib's `ComputablePred`, with respect to the explicit Gödel numbering
  `LieTerm.encode : LieTerm → ℕ` (a bijection built from `Nat.pair` and arithmetic), which
  makes `LieTerm` a `Denumerable`, hence `Primcodable`, type.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/
namespace Kourovka.«2.40»

justification.name: Kourovka.«2.40».LieTerm (with LieTerm.eval)

blocks.name: LieTerm
blocks.text:
/-- Terms in the signature $(0, -, +, [\,\cdot,\cdot\,])$ of Lie rings, with variables
$x_0, x_1, x_2, \dots$ indexed by `ℕ`. -/
inductive LieTerm : Type
  /-- The variable $x_n$. -/
  | var : ℕ → LieTerm
  /-- The constant $0$. -/
  | zero : LieTerm
  /-- The additive inverse $-t$. -/
  | neg : LieTerm → LieTerm
  /-- The sum $s + t$. -/
  | add : LieTerm → LieTerm → LieTerm
  /-- The Lie bracket $[s, t]$. -/
  | bracket : LieTerm → LieTerm → LieTerm
namespace LieTerm

blocks.code:
def eval {L : Type*} [LieRing L] (v : ℕ → L) : LieTerm → L
  | var n => v n
  | zero => 0
  | neg t => -eval v t
  | add s t => eval v s + eval v t
  | bracket s t => ⁅eval v s, eval v t⁆
blocks.docstring: The value of a term in a Lie ring `L` under the assignment `v` of the variables.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Mathlib `FreeLieAlgebra ℤ ℕ` (a quotient type with no effective encoding, so decidability cannot be stated faithfully) and `FirstOrder.Language.Term` (would still need a bespoke Lie-ring language plus an `Encodable` instance for its symbols; Mathlib has no `Primcodable` for terms, see the TODO in ModelTheory/Encoding.lean).
justification.name: Kourovka.«2.40».LieTerm (with LieTerm.eval)
justification.why_needed: Identities are syntactic objects (equations between terms in the language 0, -, +, ⁅·,·⁆ of Lie rings) and their validity must be evaluated in an arbitrary `LieRing`. No Lie-ring term syntax exists in Mathlib.

blocks.name: eval
blocks.text:
/-- The value of a term in a Lie ring `L` under the assignment `v` of the variables. -/
def eval {L : Type*} [LieRing L] (v : ℕ → L) : LieTerm → L
  | var n => v n
  | zero => 0
  | neg t => -eval v t
  | add s t => eval v s + eval v t
  | bracket s t => ⁅eval v s, eval v t⁆

blocks.code:
def encode : LieTerm → ℕ
  | zero => 0
  | var n => 4 * n + 1
  | neg t => 4 * encode t + 2
  | add s t => 4 * Nat.pair (encode s) (encode t) + 3
  | bracket s t => 4 * Nat.pair (encode s) (encode t) + 4
blocks.docstring: An explicit Gödel numbering of Lie terms, using `Nat.pair` for the binary constructors.

justification.name: Kourovka.«2.40».LieTerm.encode / decode / equivNat and the `Denumerable LieTerm` instance
justification.why_needed: `ComputablePred` requires `Primcodable`. An explicit primitive-recursive bijection `LieTerm ≃ ℕ` (built from `Nat.pair`, `/ 4`, `% 4`) gives a `Denumerable`, hence `Primcodable`, instance whose coding is transparently effective, so 'non-decidable' has its standard meaning. A choice-based `Encodable.ofCountable`/`Denumerable.ofEncodableOfInfinite` instance was rejected as it would make computability depend on an arbitrary injection.

blocks.name: encode
blocks.text:
/-- An explicit Gödel numbering of Lie terms, using `Nat.pair` for the binary constructors. -/
def encode : LieTerm → ℕ
  | zero => 0
  | var n => 4 * n + 1
  | neg t => 4 * encode t + 2
  | add s t => 4 * Nat.pair (encode s) (encode t) + 3
  | bracket s t => 4 * Nat.pair (encode s) (encode t) + 4

blocks.code:
def ofNat : ℕ → LieTerm
  | 0 => zero
  | n + 1 =>
    match n % 4 with
    | 0 => var (n / 4)
    | 1 => neg (ofNat (n / 4))
    | 2 => add (ofNat (n / 4).unpair.1) (ofNat (n / 4).unpair.2)
    | _ => bracket (ofNat (n / 4).unpair.1) (ofNat (n / 4).unpair.2)
decreasing_by all_goals
  have h1 := Nat.unpair_left_le (n / 4)
  have h2 := Nat.unpair_right_le (n / 4)
  have h3 := Nat.div_le_self n 4
  omega
blocks.docstring: The inverse of the Gödel numbering `LieTerm.encode`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `FreeLieAlgebra ℤ ℕ` (a quotient, no encoding/Primcodable and not syntactic); `FirstOrder.Language.Term` from Mathlib.ModelTheory (only `Encodable`, not `Primcodable`, and would need a bespoke language anyway); Mathlib's `deriving Encodable` handler (explicitly opaque encoding, not Primcodable).
justification.name: Kourovka.«2.40».LieTerm (with LieTerm.eval, LieTerm.toNat, LieTerm.ofNat, Denumerable instance)
justification.why_needed: A syntactic type of terms in the signature of Lie rings is needed to talk about identities as objects of a computability question; the Denumerable/Primcodable structure is needed for `ComputablePred`.

blocks.name: ofNat
blocks.text:
/-- The inverse of the Gödel numbering `LieTerm.encode`. -/
def ofNat : ℕ → LieTerm
  | 0 => zero
  | n + 1 =>
    match n % 4 with
    | 0 => var (n / 4)
    | 1 => neg (ofNat (n / 4))
    | 2 => add (ofNat (n / 4).unpair.1) (ofNat (n / 4).unpair.2)
    | _ => bracket (ofNat (n / 4).unpair.1) (ofNat (n / 4).unpair.2)
decreasing_by all_goals
  have h1 := Nat.unpair_left_le (n / 4)
  have h2 := Nat.unpair_right_le (n / 4)
  have h3 := Nat.div_le_self n 4
  omega

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 3 8 17]
theorem ofNat_encode : ∀ t, ofNat (encode t) = t
  | zero => by simp [encode, ofNat]
  | var n => by simp [encode, ofNat]
  | neg t => by
    have := ofNat_encode t
    simp [encode, ofNat, Nat.mul_add_div, this]
  | add s t => by
    have := ofNat_encode s
    have := ofNat_encode t
    simp [encode, ofNat, Nat.mul_add_div, *]
  | bracket s t => by
    have := ofNat_encode s
    have := ofNat_encode t
    simp [encode, ofNat, Nat.mul_add_div, *]
blocks.name: ofNat_encode
blocks.text:
/-- `LieTerm.ofNat` is a left inverse of `LieTerm.encode`. -/
@[category API, AMS 3 8 17]
theorem ofNat_encode : ∀ t, ofNat (encode t) = t
  | zero => by simp [encode, ofNat]
  | var n => by simp [encode, ofNat]
  | neg t => by
    have := ofNat_encode t
    simp [encode, ofNat, Nat.mul_add_div, this]
  | add s t => by
    have := ofNat_encode s
    have := ofNat_encode t
    simp [encode, ofNat, Nat.mul_add_div, *]
  | bracket s t => by
    have := ofNat_encode s
    have := ofNat_encode t
    simp [encode, ofNat, Nat.mul_add_div, *]

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 3 8 17]
theorem encode_ofNat : ∀ n, encode (ofNat n) = n
  | 0 => by simp [ofNat, encode]
  | n + 1 => by
    have h1 := Nat.unpair_left_le (n / 4)
    have h2 := Nat.unpair_right_le (n / 4)
    have h3 := Nat.div_le_self n 4
    have IH := encode_ofNat (n / 4)
    have IH1 := encode_ofNat (n / 4).unpair.1
    have IH2 := encode_ofNat (n / 4).unpair.2
    have h := Nat.div_add_mod n 4
    rw [ofNat]
    rcases (by omega : n % 4 = 0 ∨ n % 4 = 1 ∨ n % 4 = 2 ∨ n % 4 = 3) with
      h0 | h1 | h2 | h3 <;> simp [*, encode] <;> omega
decreasing_by all_goals omega
blocks.name: encode_ofNat
blocks.text:
/-- `LieTerm.ofNat` is a right inverse of `LieTerm.encode`. -/
@[category API, AMS 3 8 17]
theorem encode_ofNat : ∀ n, encode (ofNat n) = n
  | 0 => by simp [ofNat, encode]
  | n + 1 => by
    have h1 := Nat.unpair_left_le (n / 4)
    have h2 := Nat.unpair_right_le (n / 4)
    have h3 := Nat.div_le_self n 4
    have IH := encode_ofNat (n / 4)
    have IH1 := encode_ofNat (n / 4).unpair.1
    have IH2 := encode_ofNat (n / 4).unpair.2
    have h := Nat.div_add_mod n 4
    rw [ofNat]
    rcases (by omega : n % 4 = 0 ∨ n % 4 = 1 ∨ n % 4 = 2 ∨ n % 4 = 3) with
      h0 | h1 | h2 | h3 <;> simp [*, encode] <;> omega
decreasing_by all_goals omega

blocks.code:
instance : Denumerable LieTerm :=
  Denumerable.mk' ⟨encode, ofNat, ofNat_encode, encode_ofNat⟩
blocks.docstring:
Lie terms are in explicit computable bijection with `ℕ`. In particular `LieTerm` is
`Primcodable`, so `ComputablePred` makes sense for sets of identities.
blocks.text:
/-- Lie terms are in explicit computable bijection with `ℕ`. In particular `LieTerm` is
`Primcodable`, so `ComputablePred` makes sense for sets of identities. -/
instance : Denumerable LieTerm :=
  Denumerable.mk' ⟨encode, ofNat, ofNat_encode, encode_ofNat⟩
end LieTerm

blocks.docstring: An identity $s = t$ between Lie terms, represented by the pair `(s, t)`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `FirstOrder.Language.Formula.Realize`/`Theory.Model` for a bespoke first-order language; more machinery for no gain in faithfulness.
justification.name: Kourovka.«2.40».LieIdentity and LieIdentity.HoldsIn
justification.why_needed: An identity `s = t` is represented as the pair `(s, t)`; `HoldsIn L p` says both sides agree under every assignment `ℕ → L` of the variables (the universal closure).

blocks.name: LieIdentity
blocks.text:
/-- An identity $s = t$ between Lie terms, represented by the pair `(s, t)`. -/
abbrev LieIdentity := LieTerm × LieTerm

blocks.code:
def LieIdentity.HoldsIn (L : Type*) [LieRing L] (e : LieIdentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ v : ℕ → L, e.1.eval v = e.2.eval v
blocks.docstring:
The identity `e = (s, t)`, read as $s = t$, holds in the Lie ring `L`: the terms `s` and `t`
take the same value under every assignment of the variables.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `FirstOrder.Language.Formula.Realize`/`Theory.Model` for a bespoke first-order language; more machinery for no gain in faithfulness.
justification.name: Kourovka.«2.40».LieIdentity and LieIdentity.HoldsIn
justification.why_needed: An identity `s = t` is represented as the pair `(s, t)`; `HoldsIn L p` says both sides agree under every assignment `ℕ → L` of the variables (the universal closure).

blocks.name: LieIdentity.HoldsIn
blocks.text:
/-- The identity `e = (s, t)`, read as $s = t$, holds in the Lie ring `L`: the terms `s` and `t`
take the same value under every assignment of the variables. -/
def LieIdentity.HoldsIn (L : Type*) [LieRing L] (e : LieIdentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ v : ℕ → L, e.1.eval v = e.2.eval v

blocks.code:
def variety (S : Set LieIdentity) (L : Type) [LieRing L] : Prop :=
  ∀ e ∈ S, LieIdentity.HoldsIn L e
blocks.docstring:
The variety of Lie rings defined by the set `S` of identities: the class of all Lie rings
in which every identity of `S` holds.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `FirstOrder.Language.Theory.ModelType` / `Theory.Model`; not applicable to `LieRing`-structured types without a compatibility layer.
justification.name: Kourovka.«2.40».variety
justification.why_needed: The class of all Lie rings (in `Type`) satisfying every identity in a set `S`, i.e. the variety axiomatized by `S`. Applied to a `Finset` it is exactly a finitely axiomatizable variety of Lie rings.

blocks.name: variety
blocks.text:
/-- The variety of Lie rings defined by the set `S` of identities: the class of all Lie rings
in which every identity of `S` holds. -/
def variety (S : Set LieIdentity) (L : Type) [LieRing L] : Prop :=
  ∀ e ∈ S, LieIdentity.HoldsIn L e

blocks.code:
def iTheory (K : (L : Type) → [LieRing L] → Prop) : Set LieIdentity :=
  {e | ∀ (L : Type) [LieRing L], K L → LieIdentity.HoldsIn L e}
blocks.docstring:
The $I$-theory of a class `K` of Lie rings: the set of all identities that hold in every
Lie ring of the class.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `FirstOrder.Language.completeTheory` (for a single structure, first-order sentences, and requires an `L.Structure`), not the equational theory of a class.
justification.name: Kourovka.«2.40».iTheory
justification.why_needed: The I-theory of a class `K` of Lie rings: the set of identities valid in every member of `K`, following the notebook's definition verbatim.

blocks.name: iTheory

blocks.code:
@[category research open, AMS 3 8 17]
theorem kourovka.«2.40».parts.c : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ S : Finset LieIdentity, ¬ ComputablePred (· ∈ iTheory (variety S)) := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
Does there exist a finitely axiomatizable variety of Lie rings whose $I$-theory is
non-decidable?

That is, is there a finite set $S$ of identities in the signature $(0, -, +, [\,\cdot,\cdot\,])$
of Lie rings such that the set of all identities valid in every Lie ring satisfying $S$ is not
a computable (recursive) set of identities?

@[category test, AMS 3 8 17]
theorem var_var_not_mem_iTheory_variety_empty :
    (LieTerm.var 0, LieTerm.var 1) ∉ iTheory (variety ∅) := by
  intro h
  have := h ℤ (fun _ h => h.elim) (fun n => (n : ℤ))
  simp [LieTerm.eval] at this

theorem bracket_bracket_mem_iTheory_abelian :
    (LieTerm.bracket (.bracket (.var 0) (.var 1)) (.var 2), LieTerm.zero) ∈
      iTheory (variety {(LieTerm.bracket (.var 0) (.var 1), LieTerm.zero)}) := by

claims.decomposer_note: Yes/no existence question: ∃ a variety of Lie rings (Lie algebras over ℤ, i.e. abelian groups with a bilinear, alternating bracket satisfying Jacobi) defined by finitely many identities, whose I-theory — the set of all identities (equations between Lie-ring terms, universally quantified) valid in every member of the variety — is not recursive/decidable; the definitional sentence on I-/Q-theory is a preliminary, and the trailing Remark (recursively axiomatizable semigroup variety) is context, not a question; the items (1),(2),(ii) and parts a),b) absent from the statement were solved and must not be added; formalization needs an encoding of Lie terms/identities and a computability notion (e.g. ¬ ComputablePred on a countable encoding).
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same mathematical content correctly: answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ finite set S of Lie-ring identities such that the set of identities valid in every Mathlib `LieRing` satisfying S is not `ComputablePred`. c07 (structure identical to c03/c08) was chosen as the base because it mirrors the notebook's own definitions most literally: a `variety S` of Lie rings given by a set of identities and the `iTheory` of an arbitrary class of Lie rings, with identities as pairs of syntactic `LieTerm`s (signature 0, −, +, bracket; ℕ-indexed variables) and an explicit, visibly primitive-recursive Gödel numbering `LieTerm ≃ ℕ` (checked by a `rfl` test that `Encodable.encode` is this numbering). c07 as submitted fails the repository's real build (`lake --wfail build` reports missing `category`/`AMS` attributes on `decode_encode`/`encode_decode`); the final file replaces its encoding block with c04's equivalent but shorter, properly tagged `encode`/`ofNat` lemmas, adds constructor docstrings (c03/c04 style), and keeps c07's/c04's/c03's small tests. Verified: compiles standalone with only the `sorry` warning, and builds with `--wfail` inside FormalConjectures/Kourovka with all repository linters enabled.

semigroups with identity whose $I$-theory is non-recursive (see also A. I. Mal'cev,
*Mat. Sbornik*, **69**, no. 1 (1966), 3–12 (Russian)).

The labels (3) and (i) are the notebook's item numbers. Only this item of Problem 2.40 is still
open; the other parts and items of the problem have been solved and are not stated here.

## Formalisation

* A Lie ring is a `LieRing` in the sense of Mathlib: an additive commutative group with a
  biadditive bracket that vanishes on the diagonal and satisfies the Jacobi (Leibniz) identity,
  i.e. a Lie algebra over $\mathbb{Z}$.
* `LieTerm` is the type of terms in the signature $(0, -, +, [\,\cdot,\cdot\,])$ of Lie rings,
  with variables $x_0, x_1, x_2, \dots$ indexed by `ℕ`. An *identity* is a pair of terms
  $(s, t)$, read as the universally quantified equation $s = t$; it *holds* in a Lie ring $L$
  if $s$ and $t$ take the same value in $L$ under every assignment of the variables.
* The *variety* defined by a set $S$ of identities is the class of Lie rings in which every
  identity of $S$ holds (`variety`); it is *finitely axiomatizable* when $S$ is finite.
* The *$I$-theory* of a class $\mathfrak{K}$ of Lie rings is the set of identities that hold in
  every member of $\mathfrak{K}$ (`iTheory`). The class is quantified over Lie rings in `Type`;
  for identities this loses nothing, since an identity that fails in some Lie ring already
  fails in the countable Lie subring generated by the witnesses.
* Decidability is Mathlib's `ComputablePred`, with respect to the explicit Gödel numbering
  `LieTerm.encode : LieTerm → ℕ` (a bijection built from `Nat.pair` and arithmetic), which
  makes `LieTerm` a `Denumerable`, hence `Primcodable`, type.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«2.40»

/-- Terms in the signature $(0, -, +, [\,\cdot,\cdot\,])$ of Lie rings, with variables
$x_0, x_1, x_2, \dots$ indexed by `ℕ`. -/
inductive LieTerm : Type
  /-- The variable $x_n$. -/
  | var : ℕ → LieTerm
  /-- The constant $0$. -/
  | zero : LieTerm
  /-- The additive inverse $-t$. -/
  | neg : LieTerm → LieTerm
  /-- The sum $s + t$. -/
  | add : LieTerm → LieTerm → LieTerm
  /-- The Lie bracket $[s, t]$. -/
  | bracket : LieTerm → LieTerm → LieTerm

namespace LieTerm

/-- The value of a term in a Lie ring `L` under the assignment `v` of the variables. -/
def eval {L : Type*} [LieRing L] (v : ℕ → L) : LieTerm → L
  | var n => v n
  | zero => 0
  | neg t => -eval v t
  | add s t => eval v s + eval v t
  | bracket s t => ⁅eval v s, eval v t⁆

/-- An explicit Gödel numbering of Lie terms, using `Nat.pair` for the binary constructors. -/
def encode : LieTerm → ℕ
  | zero => 0
  | var n => 4 * n + 1
  | neg t => 4 * encode t + 2
  | add s t => 4 * Nat.pair (encode s) (encode t) + 3
  | bracket s t => 4 * Nat.pair (encode s) (encode t) + 4

/-- The inverse of the Gödel numbering `LieTerm.encode`. -/
def ofNat : ℕ → LieTerm
  | 0 => zero
  | n + 1 =>
    match n % 4 with
    | 0 => var (n / 4)
    | 1 => neg (ofNat (n / 4))
    | 2 => add (ofNat (n / 4).unpair.1) (ofNat (n / 4).unpair.2)
    | _ => bracket (ofNat (n / 4).unpair.1) (ofNat (n / 4).unpair.2)
decreasing_by all_goals
  have h1 := Nat.unpair_left_le (n / 4)
  have h2 := Nat.unpair_right_le (n / 4)
  have h3 := Nat.div_le_self n 4
  omega

/-- `LieTerm.ofNat` is a left inverse of `LieTerm.encode`. -/
@[category API, AMS 3 8 17]
theorem ofNat_encode : ∀ t, ofNat (encode t) = t
  | zero => by simp [encode, ofNat]
  | var n => by simp [encode, ofNat]
  | neg t => by
    have := ofNat_encode t
    simp [encode, ofNat, Nat.mul_add_div, this]
  | add s t => by
    have := ofNat_encode s
    have := ofNat_encode t
    simp [encode, ofNat, Nat.mul_add_div, *]
  | bracket s t => by
    have := ofNat_encode s
    have := ofNat_encode t
    simp [encode, ofNat, Nat.mul_add_div, *]

/-- `LieTerm.ofNat` is a right inverse of `LieTerm.encode`. -/
@[category API, AMS 3 8 17]
theorem encode_ofNat : ∀ n, encode (ofNat n) = n
  | 0 => by simp [ofNat, encode]
  | n + 1 => by
    have h1 := Nat.unpair_left_le (n / 4)
    have h2 := Nat.unpair_right_le (n / 4)
    have h3 := Nat.div_le_self n 4
    have IH := encode_ofNat (n / 4)
    have IH1 := encode_ofNat (n / 4).unpair.1
    have IH2 := encode_ofNat (n / 4).unpair.2
    have h := Nat.div_add_mod n 4
    rw [ofNat]
    rcases (by omega : n % 4 = 0 ∨ n % 4 = 1 ∨ n % 4 = 2 ∨ n % 4 = 3) with
      h0 | h1 | h2 | h3 <;> simp [*, encode] <;> omega
decreasing_by all_goals omega

/-- Lie terms are in explicit computable bijection with `ℕ`. In particular `LieTerm` is
`Primcodable`, so `ComputablePred` makes sense for sets of identities. -/
instance : Denumerable LieTerm :=
  Denumerable.mk' ⟨encode, ofNat, ofNat_encode, encode_ofNat⟩

end LieTerm

/-- An identity $s = t$ between Lie terms, represented by the pair `(s, t)`. -/
abbrev LieIdentity := LieTerm × LieTerm

/-- The identity `e = (s, t)`, read as $s = t$, holds in the Lie ring `L`: the terms `s` and `t`
take the same value under every assignment of the variables. -/
def LieIdentity.HoldsIn (L : Type*) [LieRing L] (e : LieIdentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ v : ℕ → L, e.1.eval v = e.2.eval v

/-- The variety of Lie rings defined by the set `S` of identities: the class of all Lie rings
in which every identity of `S` holds. -/
def variety (S : Set LieIdentity) (L : Type) [LieRing L] : Prop :=
  ∀ e ∈ S, LieIdentity.HoldsIn L e

/-- The $I$-theory of a class `K` of Lie rings: the set of all identities that hold in every
Lie ring of the class. -/
def iTheory (K : (L : Type) → [LieRing L] → Prop) : Set LieIdentity :=
  {e | ∀ (L : Type) [LieRing L], K L → LieIdentity.HoldsIn L e}

/--
Does there exist a finitely axiomatizable variety of Lie rings whose $I$-theory is
non-decidable?

That is, is there a finite set $S$ of identities in the signature $(0, -, +, [\,\cdot,\cdot\,])$
of Lie rings such that the set of all identities valid in every Lie ring satisfying $S$ is not
a computable (recursive) set of identities?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3 8 17]
theorem kourovka.«2.40».parts.c : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ S : Finset LieIdentity, ¬ ComputablePred (· ∈ iTheory (variety S)) := by
  sorry

/-- The `Encodable` (hence `Primcodable`) instance on `LieTerm` used in `ComputablePred` is the
explicit Gödel numbering `LieTerm.encode`. -/
@[category test, AMS 3 8 17]
theorem encodable_encode_eq_encode (t : LieTerm) : Encodable.encode t = t.encode :=
  rfl

/-- The identity $[x_0, x_0] = 0$ is in the $I$-theory of every class of Lie rings. -/
@[category test, AMS 3 8 17]
theorem bracket_self_mem_iTheory (K : (L : Type) → [LieRing L] → Prop) :
    (LieTerm.bracket (.var 0) (.var 0), LieTerm.zero) ∈ iTheory K :=
  fun _ _ _ _ => lie_self _

/-- The identity $x_0 = x_1$ fails in the Lie ring $\mathbb{Z}$, so it is not in the $I$-theory
of the variety of all Lie rings. -/
@[category test, AMS 3 8 17]
theorem var_var_not_mem_iTheory_variety_empty :
    (LieTerm.var 0, LieTerm.var 1) ∉ iTheory (variety ∅) := by
  intro h
  have := h ℤ (fun _ h => h.elim) (fun n => (n : ℤ))
  simp [LieTerm.eval] at this

/-- The defining identities of a variety belong to its $I$-theory. -/
@[category API, AMS 3 8 17]
theorem subset_iTheory_variety (S : Set LieIdentity) : S ⊆ iTheory (variety S) :=
  fun _ he _ _ hL => hL _ he

/-- In the variety of abelian Lie rings, defined by $[x_0, x_1] = 0$, the identity
$[[x_0, x_1], x_2] = 0$ is valid. -/
@[category test, AMS 3 8 17]
theorem bracket_bracket_mem_iTheory_abelian :
    (LieTerm.bracket (.bracket (.var 0) (.var 1)) (.var 2), LieTerm.zero) ∈
      iTheory (variety {(LieTerm.bracket (.var 0) (.var 1), LieTerm.zero)}) := by
  intro L _ hL v
  have h := hL _ rfl (fun i => if i = 0 then ⁅v 0, v 1⁆ else v 2)
  simpa [LieTerm.eval] using h

end Kourovka.«2.40»

items: Lie rings are Mathlib `LieRing`s (AddCommGroup with bilinear bracket, `⁅x,x⁆ = 0`, Leibniz/Jacobi); this matches the classical notion of a Lie ring = Lie algebra over ℤ.

The class of Lie rings is quantified over `L : Type` (universe 0), as in other Kourovka files. This does not change the I-theory: any failure of an identity in a larger Lie ring already occurs in the countable subring generated by the witnesses.

A 'finitely axiomatizable variety of Lie rings' is modeled as the equational class of a `Finset` of identities. Every such class is a variety (Birkhoff), and by compactness a variety that is finitely axiomatizable by first-order sentences is defined by finitely many identities, so the two readings agree.
Identities are equations `s = t` between terms in the signature `(0, -, +, ⁅·,·⁆)` with variables indexed by ℕ, represented as pairs of terms; validity is the universal closure over all assignments.

'Non-decidable' is `¬ ComputablePred` with respect to an explicit bijection `LieTerm ≃ ℕ` built from `Nat.pair` and arithmetic; a test theorem checks by `rfl` that the `Encodable`/`Primcodable` instance actually used is this numbering. The claim that the coding is primitive recursive is meta-level (standard), not proved in Lean.
The Remark about semigroup varieties and the solved parts a), b), (1), (2), (ii) are not formalized; the module docstring only notes that this is the only part retained in the current edition.
All bespoke definitions live in the problem file (the task allows exactly one output file); in a real PR the reusable parts (Lie terms, encoding, I-theory) could move to FormalConjecturesForMathlib.
